question: In which trimester does a weak cervix (cervical incompetence) usually lead to pregnancy loss?
explanation: When the cervix lacks strength, it tends to open silently between 18 and 22 weeks, which falls in the second trimester. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h1)

question: What is the main sign that sets cervical incompetence apart from a threatened miscarriage?

options.B: Painless opening of the cervix without contractions
options.C: Severe lower tummy cramps starting weeks early
options.D: Heavy bleeding before any tissue passes

explanation: Cervical incompetence causes the cervix to open quietly without the painful uterine contractions normally seen in miscarriages or labor. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h1)

question: Which tissue makes up the largest part of a normal, healthy cervix?
explanation: The cervix is mainly made of fibrous tissue and collagen, giving it the strength needed to hold a pregnancy securely. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h2)

question: How can past surgeries like dilation and curettage (D&C) lead to cervical incompetence?

options.A: They damage the collagen and connective tissue of the cervix
options.B: They cause strong, constant contractions of the womb
options.C: They trigger too much progesterone production early on
options.D: They permanently block the hormonal pathways of the placenta

explanation: Surgical procedures on the cervix can harm the tough collagen fibers, making it harder for the cervix to stay closed in future pregnancies. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h2)

question: What past pregnancy history is most typical of cervical incompetence?

options.A: Heavy bleeding after a long first stage of labor
options.B: Severe high blood pressure late in pregnancy
options.C: Repeated painless miscarriages in the second trimester

explanation: Losing pregnancies in the middle months without any pain or bleeding beforehand is the classic sign of a weak cervix. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h3)

question: A pregnant woman at 10 weeks mentions she had a cone biopsy two years ago. What should the midwife do?

options.A: Reassure her that past cervical surgeries have no effect
options.B: Note it as a risk factor and arrange early ultrasound monitoring
options.D: Advise her to stay on strict bed rest all pregnancy

explanation: A prior cone biopsy is a mechanical risk factor, so checking the cervical length early with an ultrasound helps keep a close, safe watch. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h3)

question: Which scan gives the most accurate measurement of cervical length in the second trimester?
explanation: Placing the ultrasound probe close to the cervix via the vagina gives a clear and precise view of its length and internal shape. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h4)

question: What does cervical 'funneling' seen on an ultrasound scan mean?

options.A: The inner opening of the cervix is opening while the outer part stays closed
options.B: The placenta is attached over the lower womb
options.C: Amniotic fluid is way above normal limits
options.D: The baby's head has dropped deep into the pelvis

explanation: Funneling happens when the upper part of the cervical canal starts to widen and form a wedge shape inside before the outer cervix opens. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h4)

question: At what gestational age is a planned cervical cerclage usually put in place?
explanation: A preventative cerclage is usually scheduled near the end of the first trimester, before the cervix has a chance to start changing. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h5)

question: What is the main job of a cervical cerclage?

options.A: To prevent bacteria from traveling up into the amniotic fluid
options.B: To help dilate the birth canal early for delivery
options.C: To stop all hormone production by the ovaries
options.D: To physically support the weak cervix and keep the pregnancy secure

explanation: A cerclage acts like a purse-string stitch to give the cervix extra physical support so it stays closed under the weight of the growing baby. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h5)

question: Which warning sign should a midwife tell a patient with a cerclage to report right away?

options.A: Mild morning sickness and food cravings
options.B: Darkening of the skin line on the belly
options.C: Gentle baby kicks felt in the abdomen
options.D: New pelvic pressure or fluid leaking

explanation: Pelvic pressure or fluid leakage can mean the stitch is failing, membranes are bulging, or labor is starting, which needs immediate medical attention. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h6)

question: Why is emotional support an important part of care for women with cervical incompetence?

options.A: Counseling takes the place of ultrasound scans
options.B: Past pregnancy losses often cause deep anxiety and fear in the current pregnancy
options.C: Stress hormones prevent the suture material from dissolving
options.D: Anxiety causes permanent damage to the muscles of the womb

explanation: Having gone through a mid-trimester loss before leaves many mothers feeling very anxious, making warm, compassionate support a key part of good midwifery care. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h6)
